title: Everyone Ignores This Boring Business, But It Makes Him $10M/Year
promo_conflict: The host runs Filterbuy and promotes its scale and model during the interview. He also names Roadie (owned by UPS) as a delivery partner. The guest does not give exact figures ('I can't disclose exact numbers'), and the '$10M/Year' in the title is not stated anywhere in the transcript.

stated_problem.quote: Not flexible, they're rigid, their pricing's high.
stated_problem.speaker: Jake

idea.name: Toilet paper / paper towel / dry wipe converter
idea.one_liner: Buys parent rolls from global mills, converts them into finished tissue, towel and dry-wipe products (stock and private label), and sells by the truckload to regional and national distributors.
idea.customer: Food service, jan-san and industrial distributors (600 partners in 15 countries); a few end users such as hotels
idea.offer: About 300 stock SKUs plus about 150 private-label SKUs, priced delivered, with flexibility and lower pricing than the big public competitors
idea.revenue_model: Wholesale product margin on half-truck and full-truck loads

key_quotes.quote: We buy the material from those mills and we source them globally.
So our customer is the distributor.
Cuz freight is such a big component on a small margin item.
I would only do that within 200 mi of my distribution center or a manufacturing center.

claims.claim: About 135 employees and 600 distribution partners across 15 countries
claims.quote: So, we have about 135 employees, 600 distribution partners across 15 different countries

claims.claim: Revenue is in the mid eight figures
claims.quote: I I'd say we're a a mid-eight-figure company.

claims.claim: A typical half-truck or full-truck order is worth $15k to $50k
claims.quote: I I like to say that could be, you know, 15 to $50,000 depending on the the, uh, the item.
We have about 300 stock SKUs that we sell, like standard items

claims.claim: Sales team of five or six account executives
claims.quote: our team consists of five five or six account executives

acquisition_channels.details: Account executives call distributors with the value proposition, product range and pricing
Trade shows and industry associations (suggested touch points)
Emailing target distributors each quarter, tracked in HubSpot (suggested)

ideas.delivery: Owned factory in Boyertown, PA converts the parent rolls. Domestic partners in New York and Miami fill gaps. Product is shipped by truckload to distributors.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold calls to businesses must be screened against CTPS. B2B prospect lists are covered by UK GDPR legitimate-interest rules.

stated_problem.quote: He hated having to go find a new customer every time he sold it.
stated_problem.speaker: Jake

idea.name: Reclaimed rag / disposable wipers (DPC)
idea.one_liner: Bought bales of reclaimed t-shirts, cut them into 20-lb boxes of rags, and sold them repeatedly to auto body shops and mechanics. Later moved into non-woven wipers.
idea.offer: Boxes of rags and non-woven wipers (consumables that are bought again)

key_quotes.quote: It was called DPC, Disposable Products Company.
So, that was built up until the late '90s and it was sold.

claims.quote: cut them up into 20-lb boxes of rags and sell them to, you know, auto bodies and mechanics.

acquisition_channels.details: Family members delivered by truck directly to shops

ideas.delivery: The family cut the rags by hand and delivered them by truck. They later used a building in Philadelphia with converting machinery.

idea.name: Filterbuy DTC air filters
idea.one_liner: A vertically integrated air filter manufacturer that sells direct to consumers through its own site, Amazon and Walmart, plus a fast-growing direct B2B channel to hospitals, hotels and schools.
idea.customer: Homeowners (DTC), plus institutions such as hospitals, hotels and school systems
idea.offer: Standard and custom-size air filters (300 SKUs in 4 MERV ratings) with next-day delivery to most of the US
idea.revenue_model: Product margin (about $2 cost vs $13 price) with heavy repeat purchasing and upfront payment

key_quotes.quote: I always tell people I'm in the logistics business, not the air filter business.
we're primarily direct to consumer, we get paid up front.
so I thought we were just going to buy all the standard sizes and cut and recap.

claims.quote: still still today 90% of our our revenue comes from um you know, e-commerce channels

claims.claim: $30-35M direct B2B this year, growing 50-80% a year
claims.quote: we we'll do about 30 or 35 million dollars direct B2B this year and that's you know, growing at you know, 50 to 80% year over year.
we have um you know, over 10 million end customer relationships

claims.claim: 70% of last month's business came from repeat customers
claims.quote: 70% of our um, business last month um, is from repeat customers

claims.quote: we manufacture our air filter for $2 and sell it for 13.
and we have um 30 outside sales people doing in the in this world

claims.claim: Nine distribution points (eight in the US, one in Canada)
claims.quote: we have nine different distribution points, eight in the US, one in Canada
we're in 550 Walmart's and we're about to expand with them.

acquisition_channels.details: Amazon and Walmart listings, plus 550 Walmart stores
Own site filterbuy.com, a brand built over 14 years
30 outside salespeople selling direct B2B to hospitals, hotels and school systems

ideas.delivery: Own factories and 9 distribution points. Filters are boxed only for the end customer. Last-mile delivery uses Roadie and DoorDash-style couriers.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Any subscription or auto-replenish model would fall under the DMCC Act subscription rules. Consumer data is covered by UK GDPR.

idea.name: Industrial supply distribution to sawmills
idea.one_liner: An industrial supply distributor (Talladega Machinery & Supply) that stocked what sawmills need, including janitorial items, earning a distribution margin.
idea.customer: The sawmill and wood products industry
idea.offer: Industrial supplies and consumables, including toilet paper

key_quotes.quote: We were an industrial supply distributor.
I couldn't afford to scale the distribution business at that point in my life.

ideas.delivery: Stocked warehouse inventory delivered to sawmills

stated_problem.quote: a lot of these guys don't know what it what it would take to build a manufacturing company.
stated_problem.speaker: Jake

idea.name: Become a tissue distributor first
idea.one_liner: Instead of starting a factory, distribute another maker's toilet paper or a private label to build a book of business, then consider manufacturing later.
idea.customer: Businesses buying janitorial and paper products
idea.offer: Resold or private-label toilet paper and paper products

key_quotes.quote: build up a book of business selling somebody else's toilet paper or even a private label.
So if they if they reach out because they're interested in the manufacturing, my advice is become a distributor first.

ideas.delivery: Buying from a manufacturer and delivering to the distributor's customers (physical stock)
ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold calls to businesses must be screened against CTPS.

idea.name: Acquiring distribution businesses
idea.one_liner: The host buys distribution businesses so he owns the end-customer relationship, which needs enough capital to fund their working capital.
idea.customer: End customers of the acquired distributors
idea.revenue_model: Distribution margin and owning customer relationships

key_quotes.quote: now I'm actually out there acquiring distribution businesses.
owning the customer relationship, the end customer relationship um is the most important thing to me.
